text.brief: During a Taiwan crisis in 2031, the crane operators at a West Coast port watch four ship-to-shore cranes freeze in mid-lift. The loads hang over an ammunition ship while the vendor's support line rings unanswered.
text.record: A joint House report of September 12, 2024 found that ZPMC supplied about 80 percent of the ship-to-shore cranes at American ports and that some carried cellular modems no one had ordered. A February 2024 executive order funded American crane production. Congress barred the Party's LOGINK logistics platform from ports the military uses.
text.reading: A crane is a computer that lifts containers. Remote maintenance channels built for convenience give the maker a second road into the port. In peacetime the road carries updates, and in a crisis it can carry a stop order. This is Stratagem 24, borrow the road to conquer Guo.
text.coreEvent: A US or allied port reports remote interference with mainland-made cargo equipment before 2034.
text.gapText: Technology Architecture. Ports bought cranes as machines and never tested them as computers.
text.fix: Make acceptance testing the gate for every connected machine. No contribution is suspect because of its source, and no untested one enters service. Crane workers are not agents.
